name: Khozema Shipchandler
current_role: CEO and board member, Twilio Inc.; director, Ethos Technologies
profile: Twilio's CEO since January 2024, succeeding co-founder Jeff Lawson. He joined Twilio as CFO in 2018, then served as COO and President of Twilio Communications. Before Twilio he spent over two decades at GE in finance and operating roles across Industrial Internet (GE Digital), Corporate Audit and Aviation.
interesting_fact: He rose from CFO (2018) to COO (2021) to President of Twilio Communications (2023) and then CEO (Jan 2024), one of the few finance chiefs to take over from a founder-CEO at a major developer-platform company.
deep_cut_fact: His GE career took him abroad: he held operating and financial roles at GE in the U.S., the Middle East and Singapore, across Industrial Internet, Corporate Audit and Aviation. He is an Indiana University Bloomington graduate.
notes: Public-company CEO; route via Twilio press office. Speaks at Twilio SIGNAL conferences.

name: Illiya I. Pesic
current_role: Director (and 10%+ shareholder), Silvaco Group, Inc. (Nasdaq: SVCO)
profile: Iliya Pesic is the son of Ivan Pesic, who founded TCAD/EDA software maker Silvaco in 1984; the family remains a major shareholder. Iliya joined Silvaco's board in 2012, served as Chair (2012-14) and Executive Chair (2014-21), stepped off the board in 2023 and rejoined it in May 2025, after Silvaco's 2024 Nasdaq IPO.
interesting_fact: Silvaco makes TCAD (technology computer-aided design) software used to simulate semiconductor processes and devices, an unusual niche of chip-design tooling; Pesic led the board as Executive Chair for seven years before the company went public.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an M.S. in electronic engineering from Tohoku University in Sendai, Japan (after a B.S. EE from Santa Clara University), and before chairing Silvaco worked as a senior process engineer in a fabrication facility in the MEMS and biomedical industries.
notes: Spelled 'Iliya' in company materials (SEC lists 'Illiya'). Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Route via Silvaco IR/press.

name: Troy Rudd
current_role: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, AECOM (NYSE: ACM)
profile: Troy Rudd has led global infrastructure consultancy AECOM as CEO since August 2020 (now also Chairman), refocusing it on professional services, advisory and program management in water, energy, transportation and buildings. He joined AECOM in 2009 and was previously its CFO; before that he was a KPMG partner for 10 years.
interesting_fact: AECOM credits his tenure with a near tripling of its market capitalization since he became CEO; the firm posted $16.1B of revenue in fiscal 2025 and works on energy and data-center-adjacent infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: A tax specialist by training, he holds a Master of Science in Taxation from Golden Gate University and a B.S. from the University of British Columbia; he sits on the Executive Board of SMU's Lyle School of Engineering and on the Sustainable Markets Initiative board.
notes: Strong fit for energy/data-center infrastructure topics. Press contact is AECOM's head of global communications as listed on 2025 releases; confirm current before use.

name: Ellen R Patterson
current_role: Senior EVP and General Counsel, Wells Fargo & Company; member of the Operating Committee
profile: Ellen Patterson has been Wells Fargo's General Counsel since March 2020, leading global legal affairs, litigation and regulatory matters and advising on corporate governance during the bank's long regulatory remediation. She was previously Group Head and General Counsel of TD Bank Group and, before that, a Simpson Thacher & Bartlett partner focused on M&A for financial institutions.
interesting_fact: American Banker profiled her as a 'Most Powerful Woman to Watch' for her role in steering Wells Fargo's legal and regulatory clean-up after the fake-accounts era.
deep_cut_fact: A Harvard College and Columbia Law School (1998) graduate, she spent about 14 years at Simpson Thacher before moving to Toronto-based TD; at Wells Fargo she is co-executive sponsor of the Women's Connection employee network.
notes: Bank GC, not an entrepreneur; low media profile and limited fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Route via Wells Fargo corporate communications (newsroom media contacts page).

name: Priya Aiyar
current_role: Chief Legal Officer, Warner Bros. Discovery (since Feb 2025)
profile: Priya Aiyar leads Warner Bros. Discovery's global legal and compliance functions, reporting to CEO David Zaslav. She was previously Chief Legal Officer of American Airlines (2022-25), where she oversaw labor relations through the post-COVID recovery; earlier she was Acting/Deputy General Counsel of the U.S. Treasury and a law-firm partner at Willkie Farr and Kellogg Huber.
interesting_fact: A Rhodes Scholar with degrees from Harvard, Oxford and Yale Law, she clerked for Judge Merrick Garland on the D.C. Circuit and then for Justice Stephen Breyer at the U.S. Supreme Court.
deep_cut_fact: Energy connection: before the Treasury (where she was Acting General Counsel, 2013-17), she served as Deputy General Counsel of the U.S. Department of Energy.
notes: Corporate lawyer, not an entrepreneur; WBD is in the midst of a corporate split/sale process, so she is unlikely to do media. Route via WBD corporate communications (wbd.com newsroom). No published press email found.

name: Ken Exner
current_role: Chief Product Officer, Elastic N.V. (NYSE: ESTC)
profile: Ken Exner has been Elastic's Chief Product Officer since August 2022, overseeing product and engineering across its search, observability, security and Search AI offerings and reporting to CEO Ash Kulkarni. Before Elastic he spent 16 years at Amazon Web Services, most recently running AWS Developer Tools.
interesting_fact: At AWS he ran a portfolio of 30+ developer-tools products used by millions, spanning infrastructure-as-code (CloudFormation, CDK), Amplify, the CodeBuild/CodePipeline DevOps suite, SDKs and CLIs.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2025 he led Elastic's acquisition of Keep, an open-source AIOps and workflow-automation startup, folding it into Elasticsearch; earlier he was the Elastic exec who welcomed the Opster team to 'make search better'.
notes: Frequent conference/keynote speaker (ElasticON, theCUBE); good fit for AI/data-infrastructure topics. Route via Elastic PR team.

name: Michael Stubblefield
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, PerkinElmer (New Mountain Capital-owned, since March 2026); Senior Advisor, New Mountain Capital
profile: Michael Stubblefield was President and CEO of life-sciences supplier Avantor from 2014 to 2025, leading it through its combination with VWR and its 2019 NYSE IPO; he stepped down in 2025 when Emmanuel Ligner succeeded him. In March 2026 he became CEO of PerkinElmer, the analytical-instruments business taken private by New Mountain Capital in 2023.
interesting_fact: After leaving Avantor he took over PerkinElmer, a nearly 90-year-old scientific-instrument brand now run as a standalone private company, and in June 2026 joined the board of the US-China Business Council.
deep_cut_fact: A chemical engineer by training, he holds a B.S. in Chemical Engineering from the University of Utah and an MBA from Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi, and earlier held leadership roles at McKinsey & Company and Celanese.
notes: Source data (Avantor CEO) is outdated: he left Avantor in Aug 2025 and is now PerkinElmer CEO. Press contact is PerkinElmer's VP Corporate Communications as named in the March 2026 release.

name: Allan P Merrill
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, Beazer Homes USA (NYSE: BZH)
profile: Allan Merrill has run Atlanta-based homebuilder Beazer Homes as CEO since 2011 (and Chairman since about 2019), after joining as CFO in 2007. A Wharton graduate, he spent about 13 years at Dillon, Read & Co./UBS heading its housing and building-materials banking group and was later EVP of corporate development at Move, Inc.
interesting_fact: Under Merrill, Beazer became the first national builder to make 100% of its new homes meet or exceed the U.S. DOE Zero Energy Ready Home standard, and it has pushed into solar communities; he has argued rooftop solar can help offset data-center-driven power demand.
deep_cut_fact: Long before running Beazer he was its banker: in 1992 he advised Beazer PLC's founder to buy another homebuilder rather than sell the U.S. business, which led to Beazer Homes' 1994 NYSE listing; his interest in housing began with a college job at a homebuilder doing land and sales work.
notes: Good energy-angle guest: zero-energy-ready homes, solar communities, grid/data-center demand. Gives media interviews (HousingWire). Route via Beazer IR (VP IR Mark Chekanow).

name: Ignacio Martinez
current_role: General Partner, Flagship Pioneering; Board Chair and co-founder, Inari (seed-design company)
profile: Ignacio Martinez co-founded Inari at Flagship Pioneering in 2016 and was its founding CEO; Inari uses AI-driven predictive design and multiplex gene editing to develop soybean, corn and wheat seeds and was valued around $2B. He became Inari's board chair in Feb 2025 and, as a Flagship general partner since 2013, leads its sustainability/agriculture company creation.
interesting_fact: He is a serial ag-tech company builder: besides Inari he co-founded CIBO Technologies and Invaio Sciences at Flagship and was on the founding team of Indigo Ag.
deep_cut_fact: Before Flagship he was a founding member and managing director of Syngenta Ventures, the agribusiness giant's corporate VC arm; he studied economics and business at Deusto University in Spain and holds an International MBA from IE (Spain) and WHU (Germany).
notes: Inari's current CEO is Lisa Safarian; Martinez is chair. Common name: identity confirmed via Inari/Flagship pages. No published press email found; route via Flagship Pioneering or Inari communications.

name: Jason Citron
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Discord (CEO 2015-April 2025; now director/adviser)
profile: Jason Citron co-founded Discord, the chat platform that grew from gamer voice chat into a mass-market community app valued around $15B. He previously founded mobile social-gaming network OpenFeint (sold to GREE for ~$104M in 2011). He stepped down as CEO in April 2025, handing over to Humam Sakhnini ahead of a planned IPO, and remains on the board.
interesting_fact: Discord began as an internal chat tool at his game studio Hammer & Chisel while it was building the mobile MOBA 'Fates Forever'; frustration with existing gamer voice apps led the team to pivot to communication software.
deep_cut_fact: He learned to code in QBasic at 13, and his first program was a text-based role-playing game; he calls Final Fantasy VI his favorite game and has said 'I was a Squaresoft fanboy, and I still am.' He was inducted into Full Sail University's Hall of Fame in 2025.
notes: Post-CEO, said he planned to catch up on a backlog of video games; more available than when CEO. Discord press inquiries via the newsroom address. Avoid child-safety hearing topics.

name: Hari Menon
current_role: Co-founder and board member, BigBasket (Tata Digital); stepped down as CEO in June 2026
profile: Hari Menon co-founded Bengaluru online grocer BigBasket in 2011 and led it as CEO for 15 years, through Tata Group's 2021 majority acquisition and its move into quick commerce. In June 2026 he handed the CEO role to Amazon India veteran Amit Nanda and remains on the board as a mentor alongside co-founder Vipul Parekh.
interesting_fact: BigBasket was his second try at e-commerce: in 1999 he and the same core team co-founded Fabmart, one of India's earliest online retailers, years before grocery e-commerce took off.
deep_cut_fact: He started BigBasket at around age 50, after a career that began in tech at Wipro, a story he told on YourStory's '100x Entrepreneur' podcast as proof that founding late is no barrier.
notes: Recently exited the CEO role (June 2026), so may be more open to podcast appearances; has done several podcasts (YourStory, Accel/Seed to Scale). No published contact found; route via BigBasket/Tata Digital corporate communications.

name: Xu Guangbin
current_role: Founder and Chairman (also listed as President/CEO), Huayun Data Group (华云数据, Chinac), Wuxi, China - current status unclear
profile: Xu Guangbin (许广彬) founded Huayun Data in 2010, a Wuxi-based Chinese cloud-computing provider offering public, private and hybrid cloud and 'xinchuang' domestic-tech infrastructure; it was listed as a ~$1B unicorn. He was its legal representative and largest individual shareholder (~13%).
interesting_fact: Before Huayun he built the cloud-computing unit at 21Vianet (世纪互联) after it acquired his company Lanmang Technology in 2007 - the business line that later ran Microsoft Azure in China.
deep_cut_fact: Per his company profile, his first venture (1998) was Yingzheng.com (赢政天下), which he described as China's largest software community, followed in 2003 by Lanmang Technology (telecom value-added services and IDC).
notes: Since 2024 Huayun has been the subject of shareholder disputes and his shares were reported frozen/auctioned (a listed shareholder stated he was not missing and was performing his duties); current role and availability uncertain. Not a recommended outreach target without further checks. Data-center/cloud relevance is high. Name has many homonyms; identity tied to Huayun.

name: Jennifer Hyman
current_role: CEO, Babylist (since Sept 2026); co-founder and former CEO of Rent the Runway
profile: Jennifer (Jenn) Hyman co-founded Rent the Runway in 2009 with Jennifer Fleiss while at Harvard Business School, building the designer-clothing rental and subscription pioneer and taking it public in 2021. She stepped down as RTR CEO in May 2026 and in September 2026 became CEO of baby-registry company Babylist, succeeding founder Natalie Gordon.
interesting_fact: She is one of the few women founders to take a venture-backed company public on Nasdaq as CEO, and Rent the Runway built one of the largest dry-cleaning and garment-logistics operations in the U.S. to power fashion rental.
deep_cut_fact: Before business school she was an in-house entrepreneur at Starwood Hotels, where she created the chain's first wedding business, a program that was featured on The Oprah Winfrey Show; she also sold online ads for WeddingChannel.com and did business development for IMG's fashion division.
notes: Very media-friendly and a frequent podcast guest. Newly in role at Babylist; best route is Babylist's press/communications team. No personal published email found.

name: Bai Xiaohong
current_role: Listed co-founder of Ucommune (优客工场; formerly UrWork); current role not found
profile: Bai Xiaohong (also written 白小红 / Xiao Hong Bai) is listed as a co-founder of Beijing coworking operator Ucommune, founded in 2015 with Mao Daqing (former Vanke executive), and is recorded as co-founding the UCOMMUNE (Beijing) Venture Investment entity with Mao in April 2015. Ucommune listed on Nasdaq via SPAC in 2020. No public biography or current role was found.
interesting_fact: Ucommune (UrWork) was one of China's fastest-growing coworking networks, reaching unicorn status within about three years of its 2015 founding.
notes: Very low public profile; only database listings (CB Insights, MarketScreener, 36Kr) name her as co-founder, with inconsistent spelling (白晓红 vs 白小红). Face of the company is founder Mao Daqing. Not a practical outreach target without more info.

name: Keith Marshall
current_role: Co-founder, CMR Surgical (Cambridge, UK); current title not publicly confirmed
profile: Keith Marshall is one of five co-founders of Cambridge Medical Robotics (renamed CMR Surgical in 2018), founded in January 2014, which developed the Versius modular robot for keyhole surgery and became a UK unicorn. A mechanical engineer, he is a named inventor on dozens of CMR patents covering the robot's design.
interesting_fact: CMR's five founders had all worked together at Cambridge consultancy Sagentia before leaving to build a smaller, portable alternative to Intuitive's da Vinci robot; a Versius robot is now exhibited in a Science Museum gallery in London.
deep_cut_fact: He co-authored a peer-reviewed paper with fellow founders Luke Hares, Paul Roberts and Mark Slack describing how structured surgeon/end-user feedback was used to shape Versius's design; earlier in his career he was a senior mechanical engineer at Xerox.
notes: Engineering co-founder with very low public profile; most media go to co-founders Martin Frost (ex-CEO) and Mark Slack. Common name: identity tied to CMR via Wikipedia/patents. Route via CMR Surgical communications.

name: Chen Pengyun
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Huasheng Haoche (花生好车), Beijing
profile: Chen Pengyun (陈鹏云) co-founded Huasheng Haoche in 2015 with Ma Xiaojun and serves as CEO; the company sells new cars online and offline to young buyers in China's third- to fifth-tier cities, mainly via direct-lease/installment products, and has been listed as a $1-2B unicorn. He is a Zhejiang University information-management graduate and serial entrepreneur.
interesting_fact: Huasheng Haoche ('Peanut Good Car') has kept the same model for eight-plus years: new-car direct leasing aimed at young consumers in lower-tier Chinese cities, a market largely ignored by traditional dealers and banks.
deep_cut_fact: Before Huasheng Haoche he had already founded an internet-finance company; he studied information management at Zhejiang University.
notes: Source label 'Huasheng ... E-commerce' refers to Huasheng Haoche (花生好车), an auto e-commerce/leasing platform. Low English-language profile; Chinese-language outreach via company would be needed.

name: Mack Flavelle
current_role: Co-founder, Dapper Labs and Big Head Club (NFT/entertainment studio); current role not confirmed
profile: Mack Flavelle is a co-creator of CryptoKitties (2017), the Ethereum collectible-cat game that popularized NFTs, and a co-founder and former Chief Creative Officer of Vancouver's Dapper Labs (Flow blockchain, NBA Top Shot), valued at ~$7.6B in 2021. He later co-founded Big Head Club, the studio behind Stoner Cats, and signed with Hollywood agency WME in 2022.
interesting_fact: CryptoKitties was so popular at its December 2017 launch that it congested the Ethereum network, and it became the template for the NFT boom.
deep_cut_fact: Explaining why he put cats on a blockchain, he told CBC Radio's Spark that crypto projects were unapproachable for ordinary people and cats were 'the regular language of the internet' - a deliberately friendly on-ramp to the technology.
notes: Experienced podcast guest (Bankless 2021, The First Mint). Most recent public news is from 2022; confirm current activities before outreach. Represented by WME for entertainment work.

name: John Capodilupo
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Throne (gut-health monitoring startup); co-founder of WHOOP
profile: John Capodilupo dropped out of Harvard after his sophomore year in 2012 to co-found WHOOP with Will Ahmed and Aurelian Nicolae, serving as CTO for about 10 years as it pioneered continuous physiological-monitoring wearables (valued ~$3.6B in 2021). He stepped down as CTO in 2022 and now co-leads Throne, which is building a continuous gut-health tracker.
interesting_fact: His new company's pitch, in his words: 'We're basically building WHOOP for your poop' - applying WHOOP-style continuous monitoring to gut and urinary health.
deep_cut_fact: He met Will Ahmed, then a senior and captain of Harvard's varsity squash team, in the Quincy House dining hall when Capodilupo was a sophomore computer-science concentrator; they were introduced by mutual friends.
notes: Writes publicly about building Throne; he has also shared a personal health story publicly, but outreach should stick to the tech/data angle. Best route via Throne.

name: Christian Raisson
current_role: Co-founder, ManoMano; member of the strategic committee (left operational co-CEO role in April 2026)
profile: Christian Raisson co-founded Paris-based ManoMano, Europe's leading online DIY/home-improvement and garden marketplace, with Philippe de Chanville in 2013; it reached a ~$2.6-3B valuation in 2021 after rounds led by General Atlantic, Eurazeo and others. In April 2026 the co-founders handed day-to-day management to new managing director Loic Derrien and moved to the strategic committee.
interesting_fact: The two founders were DIY enthusiasts frustrated by an 'old-fashioned retail industry'; ManoMano launched in France in 2013 and expanded to five more European countries within about 16 months. Raisson's mantra: 'Price, choice, advice.'
deep_cut_fact: Before ManoMano he ran the Gault&Millau restaurant guide for the Smartbox group, which is where he met co-founder Philippe de Chanville; he and de Chanville were named EDHEC 'Persons of the Year' 2023 (Raisson is EDHEC class of 1994).
notes: French founder; recently stepped back from operations (2026), may have more time for interviews. No published contact found; route via ManoMano press office.

name: Peter Mattis
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Cockroach Labs (CockroachDB)
profile: Peter Mattis co-founded Cockroach Labs in 2015 with Spencer Kimball and Ben Darnell to commercialize CockroachDB, an open-source, Spanner-inspired distributed SQL database; the company was valued at ~$5B in 2021. Earlier he spent years at Google, where he built Gmail's storage back-end and worked on Colossus, the successor to the Google File System.
interesting_fact: As UC Berkeley students in 1995, he and roommate Spencer Kimball created the GIMP image editor as a class project - one of the best-known open-source desktop applications.
deep_cut_fact: In 2019 he personally wrote and open-sourced Pebble, the Go key-value storage engine that replaced RocksDB inside CockroachDB; in a 2026 Pragmatic Engineer interview he described how AI coding models pulled him back into hands-on coding after stepping away to management from 2022-24.

public_contacts.value: Big Ideas in App Architecture (Cockroach Labs podcast)

notes: Strong data-infrastructure guest; regularly does technical podcasts (Pragmatic Engineer, Kubernetes Podcast). Route via Cockroach Labs press.
